summary: Both round-4 minors verified FIXED BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading. (1) The probedOnce mutant now DIES, and on the assertion the author claims: guarding the arithmetic-branch probe to fire only on the first step gives BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest:318 'expected: 14L but was: 55L', while the offset assertion (40) still passes -- so the COUNT is what kills it, exactly as claimed. I also ran the mirror mutant (probe SKIPPED on the first arithmetic step, fired on later ones): 'expected: 14L but was: 13L'. The exact 14 therefore pins the bound in BOTH directions -- one probe per burned epoch, no more and no fewer -- which an inequality in either direction would not. (2) 14 is exact and stable: three :sequencer:test --rerun-tasks runs green, and a full ./gradlew test green on the staged bytes. (3) The walk genuinely takes TWO arithmetic steps and does not short-circuit -- traced in my own tree with a stderr probe in the neverOpened branch and in crossFromCheckpoint: 'arithmetic step to epoch 2', 'arithmetic step to epoch 1', 'checkpoint HIT at epoch 1 upTo=MAX'. epoch4.open(3, 40) with epochs 3 and 2 empty is what produces it. (4) Nothing was perturbed: the burned-epoch test owns its own MemoryBinStore, the full build is green, and LocalSequencerFailoverTest still reads 18/46/30/58/22/52, matching ADR-0035's table line for line. (5) Rules 4-5 across the delta: no assertion was weakened -- the only assertion change is a strengthening (inequality -> isEqualTo(14L)); the rest of the delta is comments. Two minors remain, both prose and both of the shape this commit body names: a correction that left the claim it corrected standing three lines above it, and a sibling-suite inequality that the corrected sentence miscounts past.

findings.title: The correction fixed the second paragraph and left the FIRST one making the same false claim three lines above it
findings.detail: The delta rewrote lines 254-260 to 'The two cost tests in the sibling suite compare two MEASUREMENTS ... this and the burned-epoch count are the absolute numbers on the bounded path'. Immediately above it, untouched, the first paragraph still reads 'Every other cost assertion here compares two runs, which a recovery issuing six redundant requests satisfies.' That is now FALSE of this file. grep for counts() in BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest returns exactly two sites -- line 261 (isEqualTo(18L)) and line 314 (isEqualTo(14L)) -- both absolute. There is no cost assertion in this file that compares two runs. The two paragraphs sit three lines apart and disagree, and the surviving one carries a plausible argument for relaxing 14L back to a comparison. This is the fifth instance in this milestone of the shape the commit body itself names ('TWO CORRECTIONS OF MINE LEFT THE CLAIM THEY CORRECTED STANDING'), this time inside the correction. Prose only: no assertion is weakened, and every mutation I ran against 14L died.
findings.mutation: n/a -- a comment, not an assertion. Recorded because it is the exact failure mode the round-4 fix was made to remove, at the site of the fix.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session tightening or defending the burned-epoch count reads BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest:250-253 -- 'Every other cost assertion here compares two runs, which a recovery issuing six redundant requests satisfies' -- takes it at face value, and concludes isEqualTo(14L) three lines below is the odd one out rather than the second of two. It relaxes 14L to a comparison against a second measurement 'for consistency with the rest of the file'. Measured: under that relaxation the probedOnce mutant (arithmetic-branch probe guarded to fire only on the FIRST step) returns the correct offset 40 and is invisible again, which is exactly the hole round 4 opened this round to close.

findings.title: One inequality remains on the bounded path where an exact, stable count is available -- and the corrected sentence undercounts past exactly that one
findings.detail: Asked to look for a remaining assertion that leaves room, I found one, and it is the one the new sentence misses. The corrected comment says 'The two cost tests in the sibling suite compare two MEASUREMENTS'; the sibling suite has THREE cost assertions. The third, aPredecessorTOOSHORTToCheckpointStillStopsAtItsAncestorsCheckpoint, is neither a comparison of two measurements nor an absolute -- it is isLessThanOrEqualTo(30L). I instrumented it in my own tree: total=26 (gets=9 lists=4 stats=7), identical across three --rerun-tasks runs. So an exact number is available and stable, and the assertion carries four requests of slack -- on the same bounded path, and asserted by the same test that exists to reach the in-loop probe nothing else reaches. I could NOT name a mutation that survives the whole build inside that band, and say so rather than inflate this: the nearest candidate, skipping the in-loop probe on the FIRST CONTINUE hop so the walk stops one ancestor late, costs +2 stat +2 get +1 list +4 gets against -2 for the skipped probe, i.e. 33 > 30, and dies. Off-by-one hops in crossFromCheckpoint (from = sequence()-1 or sequence()+1) also live inside the slack HERE (27 and 25) and are killed only by the two absolute counts in the sibling file -- which is the argument for making this one absolute too, not against it. Latent weakness, not a live hole.
findings.mutation: Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence() - 1, upTo) in ChainReplay.crossFromCheckpoint -- re-reads one already-covered delta. Measured to cost 27 here, so THIS assertion passes; it is caught only by BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest's isEqualTo(18L) and isEqualTo(14L). isEqualTo(26L) here would kill it locally.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression adds up to four requests to the takeover crossing -- for instance an off-by-one that re-reads one already-covered delta per hop, Hop(chainEpoch, checkpoint.sequence() - 1, upTo), measured at 27 against the 26 this fixture actually issues. LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest:142 asserts isLessThanOrEqualTo(30L) and stays green. The only thing that fails is BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest's isEqualTo(18L) and isEqualTo(14L), in a different file. If a future task ever relaxes those two -- and the sentence at BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest:255-256, which undercounts the sibling suite's cost tests as 'two', is the prose that would justify doing so -- the in-loop-probe test that exists to reach the branch nothing else reaches would no longer notice the crossing getting more expensive at all.
